key_claims: Muscle cramp is a malfunctioning of the central nervous system's signaling system that determines muscle tension, causing over-tension in muscles
Graded adaptation prevents cramping - if your longest ride is 50km, a stretch target should be 60-70km, not 200km
Position changes like saddle adjustments should be made in tiny increments (0.5cm per day over 4 rides) rather than all at once to avoid cramping
Environmental changes from flat terrain (like Qatar) to mountainous climbing creates different torque stress that can cause cramping if not gradually adapted
Stretching 10-15 minutes pre-ride and isolating cramping muscles on-bike helps lubricate the nervous system pathway and ease cramps
specific_numbers: 81 kilometer - length of Letras climb in Colombia

cluster_reasoning: Muscle cramp prevention centers on nervous system signaling, position adaptation protocols, and pre-ride activation stretching—core strength & conditioning principles—with secondary coaching relevance due to graded training load progression and climbing-specific adaptation methodology.
